text: Rice blast (ចំនួគផ្កាឆូក, "chomngu phka chhouk") is one of the most confidently identified diseases in this source, caused by the fungus Pyricularia oryzae. The source describes three forms depending on where the fungus infects the plant: leaf blast (lesions on the leaf blade), node/collar blast (lesions at the joint where leaf meets stem, which can cause the stem to snap or lodge), and neck/panicle blast (infection at the neck just below the panicle, which breaks the neck and leaves the panicle empty or poorly filled). Lesions are typically spindle-shaped with a grayish center and a brown or reddish-brown border. The source specifically notes the disease shows up more on rice that has received heavy nitrogen fertilizer (សារធាទុអាសូត, "sar theatu asaot") - i.e. lush, over-fertilized crops are more vulnerable. Management pointed to by the source and standard practice: avoid one heavy nitrogen dose - split N applications following normal SSNM timing instead; keep reasonable plant spacing so air moves through the canopy; use varieties with better blast tolerance where available; and remove or destroy infected straw and stubble after harvest rather than leaving it in the field, since the fungus can carry over on residue to the next crop. If infection is already severe near heading, a registered fungicide applied strictly per its label may be needed, but nitrogen management and field sanitation are the first line of defense.
